facts.statement: Janenschia is a large, herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 145 million years ago.
facts.quote: Janenschia (named after Werner Janensch) is a genus of large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (around 155 to 145 million years ago) Tendaguru Formation of Lindi Region, Tanzania.

facts.statement: Fossils of Janenschia have been found in the Tendaguru Formation in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
facts.quote: Janenschia (named after Werner Janensch) is a genus of large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (around 155 to 145 million years ago) Tendaguru Formation of Lindi Region, Tanzania.

facts.statement: The fossils discovered by Fraas were transported to the Stuttgarter Naturaliensammlung in Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: The fossils were transported to the collection of the Stuttgarter Naturaliensammlung in Stuttgart, Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype for the species originally named Gigantosaurus robustus is the partial skeleton SMNS 12144, which consists of a right hindlimb.
facts.quote: The latter species was based on the holotype partial skeleton SMNS 12144, consisting of a right hindlimb.

facts.statement: In 1991, Rupert Wild renamed the species Janenschia to honor Werner Janensch after determining it was distinct from the genus Tornieria.
facts.quote: In 1991, German palaeontologist Rupert Wild of the Stuttgart Museum of Natural Sciences clarified the taxonomic status of G. robustus by concluding that it was generically distinct from Tornieria. He renamed it Janenschia in honor of Werner Janensch, who had studied the vertebrate fauna from Tendaguru.

facts.statement: Janenschia was originally placed in the family Titanosauridae, making it the oldest known member of Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Janenschia was placed in the family Titanosauridae, making it the oldest member of Titanosauria.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analysis suggests that Janenschia is a non-titanosauriform sauropod.
facts.quote: Recent cladistic analysis places Janenschia as a non-titanosauriform sauropod.

facts.statement: It is debated whether some specimens previously assigned to Janenschia belong to distinct genera, such as Tendaguria and Wamweracaudia.
facts.quote: A number of specimens formerly assigned to Janenschia have been recognized as distinct genera.

facts.statement: The specific name 'robusta' was chosen because of the animal's heavy build.
facts.quote: The specific name was inspired by the heavy build of the animal.
